thread:
ellie: Heads-up — onboarding run for 'ursa-chat-7b' shows a nasty quality regression after HF->Redwood conversion. ConvoBench bleu/rouge down ~10-15pts compared to raw HF run. :frowning:
cheng: ouch. any obvious diffs in tokenization or special tokens?
dan: I saw warnings during conversion about 'special_tokens_map' missing 'bos_token' and we fell back to pad+eos. that can scramble chat templates.
ellie: exact. the chat templates expect <|start|> / <|sep|> but converted to \"[CLS]\" style tokens. small snippet from convert log:
```
loader-bot: converting shard 1/3 -> OK
loader-bot: converting shard 2/3 -> OK
loader-bot: converting shard 3/3 -> WARNING: shard order mismatch (index 2 != expected 3)
ERROR: safetensors index hash mismatch for shard-0002.safetensors
```
miguel: shard order mismatch? that's weird, hub download should preserve names. do we reorder on rev-pin?
cheng: looks like our revpin fallback logic re-resolves sibling list and sorts by last-modified instead of filename — so partial reorders when HF returns siblings in different order after a republish.
dan: that would explain weight key rename symptoms too: if shard A contains some layers and we map keys expecting different shard boundaries, keys collide or missing.
ellie: consequences: token embedding matrices sometimes missing lm_head mapping and we see <unk> outputs in the first 128 tokens. metrics show higher token-level OOV.
miguel: quick mitigation: run convert with --preserve-shard-order and strict-revpin; also add a post-check comparing assembled checksum to origin. I pushed a small script: 
```bash
python -c "from safetensors import safe_open; print(list(safe_open('shard-0000.safetensors').keys())[:5])"
# compare to manifest order
```
cheng: good. also need to fix tokenizer mapping: HF 'tokenizer.json' had 'added_tokens' with ids starting at 50267; our loader remaps to contiguous range and overwrites special token ids.
dan: we should prefer HF tokenizer's 'special_tokens_map' and absolute ids when present. fallback only if missing.
loader-bot: convert-job 83042 failed with nonzero exit (code 2) — reason: assembled model checksum != expected, aborted.
ellie: can someone triage loader code path that sorts siblings? assign to @cheng
cheng: on it, will add a unit test that simulates re-ordered siblings and verifies shard concatenation order.
miguel: for immediate eval, I re-ran quantized pipeline using raw HF tarball (no conversion) and results match expected. so conversion bug is the root cause.
dan: experiments show if we preserve special token ids and keep shard order, quantization profiles (int8) don't cause the regression — so not a quant issue.
ellie: plan: 1) short-term: revert revpin fallback sorting, add strict checksum, re-run convert for the failing customer model; 2) medium: loader change to prefer HF special_tokens_map + explicit token id mapping; 3) long: add conversion audit in CI that runs a small conv->load->eval smoke test for new models.
cheng: also logging improvement: dump token-id map to conversion job log so we can quickly diff.
infra-bot: FYI deploy window 02:00-04:00 UTC tonight approved for loader fixes.
miguel: I'll prepare a hotfix PR and a post-conversion regression test for ConvoBench.
ellie: thanks — if anyone finds other models with inconsistent 'chat_template' fields (e.g., templates embedded in config.json vs external), flag them here. those collapse into same symptom set. :eyes:
cheng: noted. I'll add an integration test that loads config.json chat templates verbatim and compares tokenization output to HF tokenizer.
dan: small tip for triage: if you see a tokenization mismatch, run `python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; print(tokenizer.encode('Hello').ids)"` against both HF artifact and converted artifact; that usually shows the off-by-one special token bug quickly.
ellie: awesome. keep updates here. thanks team :thumbsup:
